audit.why: 50.63% over 869 games. The page reads EVEN with difficulty 7/10 and Kennen carry threat 8/10, which matches the mirror's re-rating (diffRating moved to 5/10 from Kennen's side, tone off favoured green). It is a genuine skill lane: he pokes and stun-kites, Sett needs one clean gap-close per wave.
audit.corrected: EVEN lane decided by Mark of the Storm stacks versus Facebreaker windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill/Skill/Skill/Kennen/Skill/Kennen/Kennen. The already-audited mirror settled the chart as Kennen / Kennen / Skill / Sett / Skill / Sett / Skill, which reverses who owns levels 4-5 and both item stages.
audit.why: The mirror is the authority the fixer enforces, and its reading is mechanically right: Kennen's 7s 950-range Q owns the first two levels, Facebreaker at 3 turns levels 4-5, and Sett's first-item all-in beats poke when Lightning Rush is down. whys[3] and whys[5] on this page already say Sett wins those stages, so the tokens were the error.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Kennen / Kennen / Skill / Sett / Skill / Sett / Skill in both layers, ratings re-scaled, and the whys that named the wrong owner for levels 2 and 3 rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers, and nothing on the page states the actual losing condition: Mark of the Storm stuns at three stacks, and Electrical Surge adds one passively every few attacks as well as on cast.
audit.why: Kennen P: 'stuns enemies he hits 3 times with his abilities.' W passively marks every few attacks and applies on-hit, so his damage scales with attack speed — armour reads the trade wrong. Q is 7s at rank 1 down to 4s at rank 5 with 950 range; Lightning Rush is 10s at rank 1 and 80 energy; Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s.
audit.corrected: Break off at two Marks. Q 7s/950 at rank 1, Rush 10s and 80 energy, R flat 120s. Build MR, not armour — his W applies on-hit and scales with attack speed.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Lightning Rush' was the only cooldown advice, with no duration for anything.
audit.why: Rush at 10s rank 1 is short enough that waiting it out is not a plan; the punishable cooldown is a whiffed Thundering Shuriken and a spent 120s R.
audit.corrected: Punish a whiffed Q inside its 7s; a burned Slicing Maelstrom buys a full two minutes.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Kennen on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Thundering Shuriken is 7s at rank 1 and reaches 950, so level 1 is his — he chips you for free before you own a gap-close. Soak the wave and take the chip.

edits.before: Q gives move speed toward Kennen and two empowered punches. Take short Q trades and back off before he can answer with Lightning Rush.
edits.after: Level 2 is still his — the shuriken outranges your step-up by a screen. Take short Q trades only in the 7s after he whiffs it, then walk out.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Kennen has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 swing to you: bank his poke as grit, catch him with Facebreaker as he steps up, and cash Haymaker before a third Mark can land.

edits.before: - Kennen Lightning Rush: matchup-defining — His escape. E-stun him when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Kennen Slicing Maelstrom: A storm around him that repeatedly damages + stuns via marks. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Thundering Shuriken (Q): 7s at rank 1, 4s at rank 5, 950 range — punish every whiff. - Lightning Rush (E): 10s at rank 1 and 80 energy, his only escape. - Slicing Maelstrom (R): flat 120s at every rank, so a spent R is a two-minute window.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Three Marks stun you — W adds one every few autos, so break off at two.

edits.before: Sett takes L2 with Q to trade back into Kennen's poke.
edits.after: Kennen keeps L2: his 7s shuriken outranges Sett's step-up.

edits.before: Kennen retakes L3 stacking W Electrical Surge and Q Marks on Sett.
edits.after: L3 is a read: his Marks stack, but Facebreaker punishes a whiffed Q.

edits.before: Level 1 favours Kennen — his Q Thundering Shuriken poke chips you before you can close. You take level 2 with Q to trade back, but at level 3 his W Electrical Surge stacking and Q poke swing it back to him if you walk in carelessly.
edits.after: Kennen owns the first two levels — Thundering Shuriken is 7s at rank 1 and reaches 950, so he chips you before you can close. Level 3 is a read: Facebreaker punishes a whiffed shuriken, but Electrical Surge stacks Marks if you walk in blind.

notes: Facebreaker (E) only stuns when enemies are on OPPOSITE sides of Sett, and the mirror found this page asserting a flat grab-stun in three places on Kennen's side. Sett's page repeats 'E-stun' throughout; the condition still is not stated anywhere here, and every field that could carry it is at its length limit. Also unverified: whether Slicing Maelstrom can be interrupted — kennen.json carries no channel flag and Riot's text does not say, so I made no claim.
